business_summary: Amazon.com Inc. operates in e-commerce and cloud. Revenue has compounded at 11.73% a year over three years and 13.18% over five. Operating margin is 20.33%, up 9.79 percentage points in three years. Borrowings are low at 0.17 times equity, and the company has had no loss-making quarters in the last four.
why_own: The case rests on double-digit revenue growth combined with a much higher operating margin (20.33%, up 9.79 points in three years), a 20.77% ROCE and low leverage. No investor documents were supplied, so there are no qualitative drivers, and the thesis relies on a few annual ratios.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate (3-year CAGR currently 11.73%).
The operating margin holds near its current 20.33% after rising 9.79 points in three years.
Returns on capital stay healthy (ROCE currently 20.77%, ROE 22.29%).
The balance sheet stays conservatively financed (debt/equity currently 0.17x, interest cover 43.79x). (warn line tightened by code from 0.5 to 0.22.)

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 8%, which would erase most of the three-year margin gain.
Debt/equity rises above 1.5x, a sharp change from the current low leverage.

risks.statement: The valuation (trailing P/E 20.94x, price/book 6.89x) cannot be compared with the stock's own history, because the P/E-vs-5-year-median figure is unavailable.

Trailing 4-quarter net profit (135,281 USD m) is far above FY25 net profit (77,670 USD m). What drives the gap has not been tested with the evidence supplied, so the P/E may rest on an earnings base that does not persist.

The 9.79 point rise in operating margin over three years could reverse. The 3-year net profit CAGR is undefined because profit was zero or negative at the start or end of the window, so the profit track record is short.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis is wrong if the earnings and margin step-up proves temporary. Trailing profit (135,281 USD m) is 74% above FY25 profit (77,670 USD m), and the cause is untested. The 20.94x P/E would be about 36x on FY25 profit, which is my own arithmetic. The thresholds are also loose: the margin break line (10%) and kill line (8%) both sit below the roughly 10.5% level three years ago, so the thesis stays INTACT even if the entire gain reverses. Debt/equity could rise nine-fold before the kill line trips. Evidence is thin: there are no documents, and the profit CAGR is undefined. What would change this view: A reconciliation showing that the trailing-versus-FY25 profit gap comes from recurring operations, together with margin thresholds reset above the three-year-ago level of about 10.5%.
